record.original_question: Let X be a weakly Čech-analytic Banach space in which every norm-open set is a countable union of sets that are differences of weakly closed sets. Must the identity map from X with its weak topology σ(X,X*) to X with its norm topology be σ-continuous, meaning a norm-pointwise limit of maps that are weak-to-norm continuous after countably many domain splittings?

evidence.quote: A norm pointwise limit of a sequence of piecewise continuous maps is called a σ-continuous map, [19].

Question 4. Let X be a weakly Cech analytic Banach space where every norm open set is a countable union of sets which are differences of closed sets for the weak topology. Doest it follow that the identity map Id : (X, σ(X, X∗)) → (X, k · k) is σ-continuous?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Recall the following definitions. A topological space $T$ is Čech-analytic if it is embedded into a complete metric space $M$ as a set obtained from Borel subsets of $M$ by the Souslin operation; equivalently, $T$ is the image of a Čech-complete space under a continuous map (in a suitable setting). A Banach space $X$ is called weakly Čech-analytic if $(X,\sigma(X,X^*))$ is Čech-analytic. A map $f$ from a topological space $S$ to a metric space $(Y,d)$ is called piecewise continuous if there exists a countable cover $\{S_n\}_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ of $S$ such that each restriction $f\restriction_{S_n}$ is continuous. A map $f:S\to Y$ is called $\sigma$-continuous if it is the pointwise limit of a sequence of piecewise continuous maps.

Let $X$ be a weakly Čech-analytic Banach space with the property that every norm-open subset of $X$ can be written as a countable union of sets each of which is the difference of two weakly closed subsets of $X$. Must the identity map
$$\mathrm{Id}:(X,\sigma(X,X^*))\longrightarrow (X,\|\cdot\|)$$
be $\sigma$-continuous?
